title: Sparsity lower bound for a quadratic threshold representation
statement: Let $n$ be even, and let $p:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be nonzero. Suppose that, after identifying each sign vector with its binary vector, the sign of $p(x)$ (with nonnegative values assigned sign $1$) equals $(-1)^{\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}x_i x_j}$, where the exponent is computed modulo $2$. Then the number of nonzero Fourier coefficients of $p$ is at least $2^{n/2}$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$p$ represents the specified complete quadratic Boolean function by thresholding at zero
